data.speaker: Usagi Kitadani
data.quote: This scene was made without writing any animation code!

data.speaker: Usagi Kitadani
data.quote: Instead, this was made in Godot's animation editor. It's a prototype showing we can make all of OO3's VN this way.

data.speaker: George Sanders
data.quote: The editor makes animations with timelines and keyframes and other clickable things. It might look familiar if you've edited videos before. (Evan hasn't!)

data.speaker: George Sanders
data.quote: This will help Evan do a better job of VN animation than last year. But more importantly, you - yes, you - can now help animate the VN without writing any code!

data.speaker: George Sanders
data.quote: There's still some code driving the project, but far less than last year. You can make entire scenes without writing any code. Here's how that works:

data.speaker: Takeshi Williamson
data.quote: Each line of dialogue shows an ID number at the bottom left of the screen. (Evan will set up all the dialogue. It's JSON data files.)

data.speaker: Takeshi Williamson
data.quote: Name your animation starting with a dialogue line's ID number. Your animation will play when the show reaches that line!

data.speaker: Usagi Kitadani
data.quote: If this sounds interesting, let Evan know you want to help! Discord: @erosson

data.speaker: Usagi Kitadani
data.quote: Here's some resources for learning Godot's animation editor. You can also open this scene in Godot to see how it was made.
